name: Sikkim
tagline: Prayer flags at 4,000 metres, with the world's third-highest peak on the horizon
hero_description: Sikkim compresses the Eastern Himalaya into one small state: from the easy-going capital Gangtok you climb in a single morning to the sacred, snow-ringed Tsomgo Lake and on to Nathula — one of the world's highest motorable passes, on the old Lhasa trade route. On clear autumn days, Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) owns the skyline.
best_time_to_visit: March to May for rhododendron blooms, or October to December for the clearest Kanchenjunga views — monsoon months (June–September) bring landslide-prone mountain roads.

top_attractions.name: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake
top_attractions.description: A sacred glacial lake at 3,753 m, about 40 km up the mountain road from Gangtok — oval, prayer-flag ringed, partly frozen through winter, with yaks saddled for rides along the shore.

top_attractions.name: Nathula Pass
top_attractions.description: At 4,310 m on the historic Lhasa trade route at the India–China border, one of the world's highest motorable passes — visited on a Protected Area Permit and closed to visitors on Mondays and Tuesdays.

top_attractions.name: Rumtek Monastery
top_attractions.description: Sikkim's largest monastery, about 23 km from Gangtok — seat-in-exile of the Karmapa lineage, where butter-lamp prayers start the day in the main hall.

top_attractions.name: Kanchenjunga viewpoints
top_attractions.description: The world's third-highest mountain (8,586 m) anchors Sikkim's horizon — Tashi Viewpoint near Gangtok catches it at sunrise, most reliably from October to December.

top_attractions.name: MG Marg, Gangtok
top_attractions.description: The capital's pedestrian-only promenade — traffic-free, litter-free by law, and lined with momo joints and cafes for the evening stroll.

top_attractions.name: Gangtok Ropeway
top_attractions.description: A cable-car ride above the capital's stacked ridgeline houses, with the Ranipool valley dropping away below.
